I am 53 years old, farming 22.5 mu here in Quzhou County for 33 years. I never spent a day in school. My father taught me, and I learned by watching the neighbors who get good harvests. My household has three people, and my son works off-farm in the city, so it is mostly me and my wife running the land. We have a well, but pumping water costs diesel money, so I count every drop.

This year I will split my land the same as last year because change is risky. I put 12 mu into wheat and then maize. For the winter wheat, I sow the improved seed I bought from the dealer — 12 jin per mu. Before sowing, I spread one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. When the wheat turns green, I topdress with 30 jin of urea per mu. I count that as about 15 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: green-up water, jointing water, and filling water. I spray pesticide twice, once for weeds and once for bugs. After the maize stalks are chopped, I hire the village tractor to rotary-till the ground. If the wind does not blow the seedlings dead, I expect 550 kg per mu.

Right after the wheat comes off in June, I plant hybrid maize on those same 12 mu. There is no time to plough — I use the no-till seeder. I put 5 jin of seed per mu. At sowing, I drop one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and at big trumpet stage I add 25 jin of urea per mu. That comes to about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, after sowing if it is dry and at jointing. Two sprays: herbicide first, then insecticide for the borers. I expect 650 kg per mu.

My cotton field is 3.5 mu. I plant hybrid cotton, about 3 jin of seed per mu. Cotton needs feeding. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress twice with 20 jin of urea each time. That is about 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I water three times and spray five times because the bollworm never sleeps. I hire the tractor to plough the cotton field deep every spring. I hope for 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Peanut takes up 3 mu. I shell my own saved seed — about 15 jin per mu. I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and add a handful of urea at flowering. Total is about 8 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I water twice and spray three times. Rotary till in spring. Should get 320 kg per mu.

Millet is on 2 mu, for our own porridge. I use my own traditional seed, less than 1 jin per mu. I spread 20 jin of compound fertilizer per mu and leave it — about 5 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium per mu. Water once if the drought comes, spray once for weeds. Plough in spring. Expect 250 kg per mu.

Mung bean is on 2 mu. I plant my own traditional seed, 3 jin per mu. Mung bean does not ask for much. I give it 15 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — about 3 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium per mu. Irrigate once when it flowers, spray once. Rotary till. Expect 100 kg per mu.

I thought about cutting fertilizer because the price went up again, but a bad harvest means losing everything. Wasting some fertilizer is just money out of pocket. I watch my neighbors — they are putting down the same amounts on wheat and maize, so I will do the same. If they had cut back, I might too, but nobody wants to take the risk. I have to balance my whole purse: more money on fertilizer means I hire less labor, but my wife and I can manage the weeding and spraying ourselves since the farm is big but not too big for us.
